Contact Us
Headteacher's welcome
Welcome to Al-Zahra School; a bastion of academic striving and spiritual serenity for the young ladies under its banner.
Vision and Mission Statement
Our namesake Sayyeda Fatima Zahra (p.b.u.h) exemplifies the excellence we pursue at Al-Zahra.
Achievements
Our average attainment scores are typically above the national average, across the school.
We look forward to welcoming you
Insipred, confident and ready.
Alumni
"I studied at ASAZ from year 1 to year 11 graduating in 2003. I then went on to study Medicine at Cambridge University and Imperial College and am currently an Academic Clinical doctor in paediatrics and genetics at Great Ormond St Hospital. I fondly remember my time at ASAZ and could not have wished for a better start to my education. The atmosphere was always warm and safe and encouraging and it filled me with a confidence that carries me till today. The teachers always believed in us and were very invested in our education."
Being a student at ASAZ was an unforgettable experience for me. The very start of my journey to education began there, joining the school in Reception and staying on till year 11. I was surrounded by teachers who wanted to see me excel and their support and encouragement drove me throughout. The school was also one of my first platforms for recitations. My sisters and I were always encouraged by the teachers to recite various poems during the special assemblies conducted in school. We have now released 12 albums and a number of singles consisting of Islamic nasheeds and eulogies, some actually inspired by what we recited as children in school. After graduating from the school, I went on to study Psychology at City University after which I acquired my PGCE from the University of Manchester. My passion for teaching stemmed from having studied at ASAZ and I was fortunate enough to go back to ASAZ as a teacher. Teaching at the school has been like a dream, knowing that I can give back to the society of today and help make a difference in the children's lives in whatever way possible.

pageCache.text:
Vision and mission statement
Our namesake Sayyeda Fatima Zahra (p.b.u.h) exemplifies the excellence we pursue at Al-Zahra. The linguistic denotation of the Arabic word 'Zahra' means 'to blossom'
Our Vision (Al-Zahra)
Our namesake Sayyeda Fatima Zahra (p.b.u.h) exemplifies the excellence we pursue at Al-Zahra. The linguistic denotation of the Arabic word ‘Zahra’ means ‘to blossom’. In this vein, our young ladies are emotionally nurtured and intellectually nourished so they may flourish into positive role models, proactive citizens and capable leaders of tomorrow.
In line with our motto “Individually we endeavour; together we shine”, Al-Zahra School’s vision is to inspire a love of learning and to foster the inherent qualities and teachings of the Qur’an and the Ahlulbait.
Our girls emerge from Al-Zahra as inspired students; conscientious citizens of their wider communities; proactive citizens in service to the wider culture of a modern, multi-facetted Britain. To this end, our ladies shall endeavour to be the best version of themselves; to invest their time wisely. The School will recognise and respect each student’s unique place in Allah’s creation, and nurture our budding learners into becoming confident, tenacious and independent thinkers who aspire to become successful individuals in an ever changing world.
We have a vision to reach our goals of excellence indented into the fabric of our existence. Our vision constitutes four key elements:
Excellence in Education
“The most helpful thing in purifying the intellect is education” – Imam Ali (a.s.) At Al-Zahra, we are keen to create an exciting learning environment for our students where we can cultivate and cherish their highest aspirations. We foster the tenets of the Ahlulbait (a.s.) according to which it is incumbent upon every Muslim to acquire knowledge and education. As such, we believe that every child has the potential to succeed within an intellectually stimulating and challenging setting. Every child is encouraged to manifest courage and enquiry in their quest for intellectual betterment. Being courageous can be monumental in the most modest of ways; having a go at a difficult question, offering an answer in a lesson, or nudging a peer in the right direction. Our girls learn and grow through the small, everyday steps they take that facilitate large, spirited leaps into their future.
Excellence in God-consciousness
“Through God-consciousness, actions become pure” – Imam Ali (a.s.) Our primary aim is to centralise God-consciousness into the psyche of each pupil, so they may develop spiritually, ethically and theologically. Al-Zahra School strives to inculcate the love of God within a positive and caring environment, as we recognise each individual as a unique component of God’s creation. We inculcate the values taught by our role models, the Ahlulbait (a.s.), to foster God-consciousness in our students.
Excellence in serving communities
“The best of mankind is the one most useful to them” – Prophet Mohammed (p.b.u.h.) Al-Zahra strives to nurture individuals who will live fruitfully in their society with conviction in themselves and empathy for others. The school has a sense of being part of a wider community, which nurtures well-rounded, compassionate individuals who are determined to mature into outstanding British citizens, beneficial to the social and economic growth of our country. Our students harbour a sense of responsibility and accountability towards themselves, their peers, families and the wider community.
Excellence in character
“The purest of all in lineage is the best of them in character” – Imam Ali (a.s.) Al-Zahra School is focused on eliciting the noble and honourable characteristics of its pupils: honesty, integrity, compassion and mutual respect – these are all traits we endeavour to instill daily and tirelessly. Tenacity, self-respect and self-belief upholds our core, and inspires each student to become paragons of patience and perseverance.
Our vision is to ensure that Al-Zahra School provides a perfect balance that caters to our pupils’ progress and attainment of high standards in order to develop caring, courteous and law-abiding citizens. Our aim is to develop and promote the academic, emotional, spiritual and physical development of every student regardless of race, creed and culture. This is achieved by teaching a diverse curriculum that embeds academic brilliance, creativity and critical thinking leading to graduates that possess outstanding moral values to become responsible citizens of the future.

Our Founder and Proprietor
The Al-Khoei Foundation is the proprietor of Al-Sadiq School and Al-Zahra School.
The Al-Khoei Foundation is the proprietor of Al-Sadiq School and Al-Zahra School. Founded in 1989 by the late spiritual leader of Shia Muslims, His Eminence Grand Ayatollah Sayed Abulqasim Al-Khoei, this international, non-profit organisation seeks to address the welfare of Muslim communities, and in particular Shia Muslims, around the world. Its fundamental aim is to promote education, intra- and interfaith dialogue, enhance the understanding of Islam and encourage citizen empowerment and community development. It has also held a general consultative status at the UN ECOSOC since 1998.
Against the backdrop of this far-reaching vision, Al-Sadiq and Al-Zahra Schools first opened their doors in 1991 and were subsequently registered as two separate schools: Al-Sadiq School and Al-Zahra School.
The schools are named after two distinguished Islamic personalities: Imam Ja’far Al-Sadiq (the sixth divinely appointed leader after the Prophet of Islam for Shia Muslims) and Sayeda Fatima Al-Zahra (daughter of Prophet Muhammad).
The Al-Khoei Foundation has founded similar educational establishments across the world, including the USA, Canada, Thailand and Pakistan.

Head Teacher's message
Named after Sayyeda Fatima Al-Zahra (p.b.u.h), the daughter of the Holy Prophet (p.b.u.h); our vision is to pursue excellence in education, unwavering God consciousness and service to the community.
Welcome to Al-Zahra School; a bastion of academic striving and spiritual serenity for the young ladies under its banner. Named after Sayyeda Fatima Al-Zahra (p.b.u.h), the daughter of the Holy Prophet (p.b.u.h); our vision is to pursue excellence in education, unwavering God consciousness and service to the community.
The teachings of the Qur’an and the Ahlulbayt are integral to our ethos and encapsulate school life. We provide a broad curriculum that is ambitious and stimulating, along with a wide range of extra-curricular and enrichment opportunities. Through all endeavours, our school nurtures dynamism and determination through the troughs and peaks of academic life. With a sense of being part of a wider family, we nurture well-rounded, cultivated and compassionate individuals who respect the differences and human dignity of others.
Our girls are driven by self-motivation, self-discipline and a common purpose. Through these years with us, they become secure in their sense of pride and belonging, buffered by a friendly and supportive school community. They leave Al-Zahra full of integrity and ambition, empowered to make waves in the world they enter. Al-Zahra welcomes visitors to personally experience the buzz and energy of the school; to interact with our personable pupils who constitute the very essence of our establishment. It is our aim to enable our girls with the most holistic experience of education, in which they may thrive and emerge as conscientious citizens of a modern, multi-facetted Britain.

ASAZS Bursary Scheme
Supporting Families, Strengthening Our Community
Al-Sadiq & Al-Zahra Schools are among the oldest and most established Shia Muslim faith schools in Europe. Founded in 1991 by Grand Ayatollah Khoei(ra), we have served the British Shia Muslim community for over three decades, nurturing two generations of pupils in faith, academic excellence, character and community service.
We recognise that for some families, the cost of an independent faith education can be a genuine barrier, particularly in the light of recent financial pressures facing many households in our community. The ASAZS Bursary Scheme has been established to ensure that financial circumstances alone do not stand between a deserving child and the education they deserve.
What Is a Bursary?
A bursary is a means-tested financial award that reduces or removes the cost of tuition fees for eligible families. While this is not a loan and there is no obligation to repay, parents are encouraged, where their circumstances permit, to support the continuation of this service to the community through voluntary donations. Awards are assessed based on financial need and family circumstances, and are reviewed annually.
Bursary awards range from a partial reduction to full remission of tuition fees, depending on assessed need.
Who Can Apply?
The Scheme is open to:
There is no restriction by year group. Applications are considered for all stages from Reception through to Year 11.
How to Apply
Applications for a bursary are handled entirely separately and confidentially from the standard admissions process. Submitting a bursary application will have no bearing on your child’s admissions assessment.Families may apply for a bursary before, during or after registering their child for a place. You may also choose to await the outcome of your bursary application before confirming your admissions registration.To apply, please complete the confidential online Bursary Application Form.
The form asks about your household circumstances and the child you are applying on behalf of. You are also welcome to upload any supporting documents at the time of submission.
Confidentiality
We take the confidentiality of all applications very seriously. Your application and its outcome will be accessible only to the school’s Bursary Committee, relevant administrative staff involved in fee processing and registration, and authorised representatives of our funding partners where required for audit or accountability purposes. In the event of an appeal, the Proprietor Trustee handling the appeal will also have access to the relevant application and decision. All parties are bound by strict confidentiality obligations. Your application will not be disclosed to other pupils, parents, or staff beyond those with a legitimate need to know.
What Happens Next?
Once your application is received, the school’s Bursary Committee will review it against our assessment framework. We may contact you to request additional information or documentation. You will be notified of the outcome in writing.
Our Policy
For full details of how the Scheme operates, including our assessment criteria, review process and appeals procedure, please read The ASAZS Bursary Scheme — Policy & Procedures.
Contact Us
If you would like to discuss your circumstances informally and in confidence before applying, please do not hesitate to contact us on bursary@asazs.co.uk. We are here to help.

Entry Procedure
Al-Zahra School accepts girls from Year 4 to Year 10. From Year 3, girls from Al-Sadiq School are automatically enrolled into Year 4 of Al-Zahra School. We encourage pupils to join at the beginning of the academic year, however in-year applications are also possible (apart from Year 11). Places are awarded on the basis of available vacancies and we will ask to see reports from previous schools.
Assessment
All applicants are assessed depending on age and the year group for which the application is being made. Primary applicants are assessed on Maths and English. Secondary applicants are assessed on Maths, English and Science. If successful, the applicant is then invited to an interview with the Headteacher.
School acceptance
Our assessment and interview process are designed to identify inquisitive and enthusiastic learners, who will thrive in our Islamic and educational environment. All applications are treated in an equal manner irrespective of origin, race and colour. Places will be offered subject to availability and whether the School feels that the child’s development is in-line with the School’s expectations.
Submit all required documents and registration fee to school office.
Pupils are required to complete assessments, as above followed by an interview with the headteacher.
Upon successful assessment and interview pupil is offered a place. An entry date is set, and one term's fees is payable prior to starting.
Contact our Admissions Officer for an initial conversation and to arrange a visit.
Mrs M Jaffer, Admissions Officer
Tel: 02073727706 Email: alzahra@asazs.co.uk
Admission forms
You can apply online and the admission office will process your application in due course.

Parent Teacher Association (PTA)
The PTA at Al-Zahra is a vibrant body of dedicated parents whose focus is to build community spirit among parents/carers and staff and raise funds for the school.
We would like to welcome all parents/guardians of Al-Zahra pupils, as members of the Parent Teacher Association (PTA). All parents and carers at Al-Zahra are automatically members of our PTA.
The PTA at Al-Zahra is a vibrant body of dedicated parents whose focus is to build community spirit among parents/carers and staff and raise funds for the school. Any funds raised are used to supplement enrichment activities for all school children, such as field trips.
Feel free to contact the PTA if you are interested in getting involved.
Al Zahra School caters for pupils from the age of 7 to 16 years old. Our school helps to develop pupils both spiritually and academically.
